answer_raw:
The highest-paying roles without a degree generally require specialized certifications, apprenticeships, or enough time on the ground to move from front-line work into management.

| Job Title | Typical Pay | Time to Entry/Path |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Commercial Pilot** | **$123,220** (as of August 2026) [5] | Requires postsecondary nondegree awards, flight training, and an FAA certificate [5]. |
| **Construction Manager** | **$155,463** (ass of January 2019) [3] | Typically involves working up from front-line roles into supervision [5]. |
| **Transportation Manager** | **>$50,980** (as of October 2026) [1] | Front-line experience followed by promotion to management [5]. |
| **Police Supervisor** | **>$50,980** (as of October 2026) [1] | Typically requires five years or more of experience in the field [5]. |
| **Firefighting Supervisor** | **>$50,980** (as of October 2026) [1] | Typically requires five years or more of experience in the field [5]. |

While the provided data lists these specific roles, it does not provide exact timelines (in months or years) for the pilot training or the specific years of experience required for the supervisor roles beyond a general "five years or more" [5]. For a more granular breakdown of the pilot training timeline, you would need to check specific flight school curricula or FAA regulatory requirements.
